claims.quote: Reader's top concern (Strait of Hormuz / Middle East Oil Shock, 8/10): a +10% weekly oil shock lowers an equal-weight basket of her holdings.
claims.test: Equal-weight total effect of do(WTI +10%) on {T, JNJ, MSFT, ORCL, AMZN, VOO} is negative
queries: returns(weekly log; ^TNX in pp) 2021-11-01..2026-10-19, n=260; model r_i ~ VOO + CL=F + ^TNX + DX-Y.NYB (Newey-West lags 2)
block_bootstrap(B=2000, block=8, seed=47); centered_pvalue, one-sided H1: stat < 0
do(): TE_i = b_oil_i + b_mkt_i * g, g = coef of CL=F in VOO ~ CL=F + ^TNX + DX-Y.NYB; adjustment set {^TNX, DX-Y.NYB}; placebo = CL=F rolled 26 weeks
claims.notes: Assumed DAG: oil -> market -> stock and oil -> stock; rates and dollar as common causes. Not identified if oil and stocks share an omitted driver (e.g. global demand).

claims.quote: The oil shock is a dual-plane signal: an unusual oil move (Echo) while the oil-to-holdings relationship has changed (Shadow).
claims.test: Echo: |oil weekly return| unusual vs 5y (N1). Shadow: any holding's 26-week oil beta unusual vs its history (N2). Both needed.
queries: returns(weekly log; ^TNX in pp) 2021-11-01..2026-10-19, n=260; model r_i ~ VOO + CL=F + ^TNX + DX-Y.NYB (Newey-West lags 2)
Echo: residual_percentile(CL=F weekly log return, demeaned); Shadow: window_percentile(beta_oil, window=26) per holding, Bonferroni x6; dual-plane p = max(p_echo, p_shadow)
claims.notes: N3 (coincidence null) and N4 (lead time) are not run for this pattern yet; a dual-plane hit here is a candidate, not an alert.
